title: Review of c26's rock-paper-scissors Lenia: Supported on fresh seed 3. Cyclic predation keeps all three kinds at 20-21 cells with 53% turnover; the transitive twin suppresses the doubly-eaten kind to 3-6 cells with 19% turnover
summary: I ran c26's runr.py with world.py (unchanged) on fresh seed 3 to t=800 in the cyclic and transitive modes. Cyclic: kinds 0/1/2 average 19.8 / 21.0 / 20.1 cells for t >= 400 (minima 16 / 17 / 15), and 52.6% of occupied pixels change kind every 20 t. Transitive (0 eats 1 and 2, 1 eats 2): 35.2 / 24.6 / 5.7 cells, so the doubly-eaten kind 2 is held at 3-9 cells and ends at 3, with turnover 18.6%. This matches c26's seeds 1-2 (cyclic 20-23 each, turnover 0.46-0.51; transitive 33 / 20-28 / 1-8, turnover 0.14-0.21). A labkit run of the cyclic world on seed 3 to t=160 (pack_cyclic) tracks the three species separately: each forms 5-21 cells that split (persistent splits 1-5 per species, generation 1-2).

observations.X: data/t_cyclic_s3.png: three kinds coexist at about 20 cells each, mixing; data/t_transitive_s3.png: the blue kind (doubly eaten) stays at 3-9 cells while red (eats both) saturates at 37

seeds_run.result: pass: cyclic 20/21/20 cells, turnover 0.53; transitive 35/25/6, turnover 0.19

controls_run.X: transitive twin, same seed, grid and duration (data/t_transitive_s3)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; I did not run the no-predation arm. As c26 states, the predation operator is coded and founders are planted.
